subject: Request: Dedicated capacity demo + throughput discussion
messages:
From: Samantha Tan <samantha.tan@avahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Interested in Dedicated capacity demo (throughput / latency)

Hi Soojin,

We signed up via the self-serve flow last week and are evaluating Dedicated capacity for a production feature. Our immediate goal is a demo that covers throughput/latency expectations and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). High-level context: we are building a clinical triage assistant and need predictable throughput during peak hours.

Quick stats:
- Pilot expected traffic: ~40 concurrent sessions at peak, 2–3 requests per session within short bursts
- Typical sequence length: ~200–350 tokens
- P95 latency target: <150ms for user-facing responses (we know token-level numbers vary)

Could we set up a 30–45 minute call this week with someone who can walk through Dedicated capacity (expected throughput, autoscaling behavior, fallback routing) and answer questions about data isolation and compliance? We're PST (San Francisco).

Thanks,
Samantha Tan
Product Ops, Ava Health
Samantha.tan@avahealth.com

--

Hi Samantha — great to hear from you and thanks for the context. I'm an SDR on the accounts team; happy to coordinate a short demo with our Solutions team focused on Dedicated capacity.

A few quick clarifying questions that will help Marissa prepare:
- Is 40 concurrent sessions your expected peak concurrency, or a sustained concurrency target over multiple minutes?
- Do your payloads include long system prompts or many context tokens (beyond the 200–350 you listed)?
- Any hard SLOs for p99 or tail latency we should be aware of?
- Would you like the call to cover deployment (VPC/private) and SOC2 evidence or focus purely on performance?

Suggested times (PST):
- Wed 2026-03-04 10:00–10:45
- Thu 2026-03-05 14:00–14:45
- Fri 2026-03-06 09:00–09:45

I attached a short "capacity_precall_checklist.pdf" to speed the prep. Can you confirm a preferred slot and we'll send a calendar invite with a brief agenda (technical + pricing / next steps)?

Best,
Soojin Lee

Hi Soojin — thanks, Thu 2026-03-05 14:00 PST works for us. A few answers:

- 40 concurrent sessions is our expected peak concurrency during office hours; bursts can spike to ~60 for short windows (1–2 minutes).
- Payloads: most prompts are user + system + 2–3 turns of history; average ~250 tokens, worst-case ~400 tokens.
- SLOs: p95 <150ms is our goal; p99 under 300ms would be ideal but not a hard blocker for the pilot.
- We definitely want to cover private deployment options (VPC) and compliance questions briefly.

We can also share a redacted sample dataset ahead of time if that helps with load projection — see attached small sample (test_dataset_sample.csv).

Thanks,
Samantha

Hi Samantha and Soojin — Marissa here (Solutions Engineer). Thanks for the sample dataset, that helps a lot. A couple of prep items so the demo is productive: 

1) Can you confirm the maximum tokens per request we should test (you mentioned worst-case ~400) and whether embeddings are requested in the same pipeline?
2) If you can grant read access to a small S3 bucket or share a Drive link for the redacted sample, I'll run the projection and prepare a short load test plan for the call.

High-level plan for the demo:
- Warm-up: show baseline latency on a small host with a warm KV cache
- Throughput projection: map your concurrency/seq-length distribution to recommended Dedicated pool size, batching config, and expected p95/p99 numbers
- Fallbacks & cost levers: quantization, reduced batch sizes for latency-sensitive routes, and cross-region fallback behavior

I'll bring example graphs and a canned Jupyter notebook we use to estimate qps vs. pool size. If you prefer us to run an early sandbox test ahead of the call we can — just need the sample data link.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
